newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors summon President Kim's aide.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors summon President Kim's aide.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors said on Monday they had summoned a close associate of President Kim Young-sam in connection with controversial loans to Hanbo Steel Co.

Prosecutors asked Hong In-gil, a member of Kim's ruling New Korea Party and until recently a senior official at the presidential Blue House, and two other politicans to appear at the prosecution office by 0500 GMT on Monday, they said.
Hong has been Kim's close associate for more than two decades.
Among the three is Kwon Roh-kap, a prominent opposition member of parliament and a top aide to opposition leader Kim Dae-jung, a prosecution official said. The other politician was not identified.

Prosecutors have questioned bankers and officials of Hanbo to find out if kickbacks were involved in huge loans to Hanbo Steel. The company, South Korea's second largest steelmaker, was declared insolvent on January 23 with five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans.
Prosecutors have arrested Chung Tae-soo, founder of the Hanbo Group, and two leading bankers over the Hanbo loan scandal.
